title: TBD Mission
description:
Mission JSON contract v1. Authored by the web wizard / hand-written, validated by the web validator, and executed by the TBD-Framework Enfusion loader. Missions reference registry aliases, never raw prefab GUIDs.

T-450 — WHOLE-DOCUMENT SIZE CEILING. `TBD_MissionLoader.MISSION_FILE_MAX_BYTES` is `8 * 1024 * 1024` (8388608) bytes (`apps/mod/tbd-framework/Scripts/Game/TBD/Backend/TBD_MissionLoader.c`). A profile file over that is refused at `LoadFromProfileFile` before `Read()`, because a truncated read would then fail JSON parse with a misleading error. JSON Schema draft 2020-12 cannot express raw byte size of an object instance, so the ceiling is declared here as `x-tbd-missionFileMaxBytes` and enforced by `validate_mission_document` (API `GET /missions/:id/compiled`) and `xtask schema validate` (which also cross-checks the mod constant). A soft description alone is not a pin.

schemaVersion.description: 1.1 adds required slots[] for per-player spawn positions. 1.2 adds the optional per-slot y (spawn height, metres ASL). 1.3 widens the WIRE once for the whole editor program (T-706): objectives[], variants, marker style/area, per-slot uid already present, vehicles[], editorTriggers[], per-squad waypoints/AI state, placement scatter, vehicle/entity states, environment, missionParams[], zone-volume + attacker/defender + startingOwner rules, play-area vehicleClasses, per-slot gadgets. Every 1.3 addition is OPTIONAL and ADDITIVE — `JsonLoadContext` ignores unknown keys, so the WIRE SHAPE of a 1.1/1.2 document is unchanged and the bump exists to NAME the widening, not to reshape it. THE MOD ACCEPTS "1.3" SINCE 2026-09-06 (e5f46e4fc): both copies of `TBD_MissionValidator.c` (tbd-framework and tbd-export) declare SCHEMA_1_3 and `CheckSchemaVersion` admits it, compile-verified since T-946.3 unblocked the mod gate. `flatten.rs` EMITS 1.3, and only when a 1.3 key actually reaches the wire: T-674.1 latches on emitted slot identity and `leaderSlotId`, T-675.1 on a non-empty `vehicles[]`. A document with no 1.3 key still emits 1.1/1.2, so old servers are unaffected. The latch must stay on the SERIALISED value, never the resolved one — T-946.11 is the shape where the version claims 1.3 and no key is on the wire. Like 1.1/1.2, a 1.3 document still requires slots[]. THE READERS ARE MOD-SIDE AND LAND SEPARATELY: most 1.3 fields are carried on the wire and read by nothing on any build shipped today (the `xtask schema validate` unread-fields gate asserts exactly that, per field, and names the ticket that will land each reader; a field whose reader has landed loses its row rather than keeping a re-pinned one). `editorTriggers`/`activation`/`effects`/`variantId` are the first to have lost theirs, to T-676's trigger runtime. Do not cite a 1.3 field as a capability — it is a definition ahead of its consumer, the same discipline the top-level `entities` description states.

slots.description: Flattened ORBAT slot instances with exact spawn positions (required for schemaVersion 1.1).

entities.description:
World objects the MISSION places itself — vehicles, compositions, props — each named by a registry alias.

NOTHING READS THIS ON ANY BUILD SHIPPED TODAY, and a green validator is not evidence otherwise. `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` (TBD_MissionLoader.c) declares no `entities` field, so the loader parses a mission and drops this array on the floor; no code path in the mod spawns a mission entity; `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.ArmDestroyTargets` states this in its own header and reports a destroy objective that finds no target as a first-class DIAGNOSTIC rather than faking one (TBD_ObjectivesComponent.AdvanceDestroy repeats the warning); and the editor's vehicle row is `{id, resourceName, position, squadId}` (map-engine-core doc/store.rs `add_vehicle`) with nowhere to author contents. This array is a CONTRACT AHEAD OF ITS CONSUMER — legitimate, because the schema is the shared definition the mod, the API and the editor each build against, and defining it here is what lets those three land in any order — but it is a definition, not a capability. Do not cite it as a feature.

layers.description: Tier 2 decoration layer aliases attached to this mission.

tasks.description:
T-936.2 — authored TASKS with a real state machine (schemaVersion 1.3). Distinct from `objectives[]` (T-212: the mission's typed objective SUBJECT) and from `winConditions.endOn` (the round-end TRIGGER vocabulary). A task is what the HUD and the briefing's My Tasks list show: a primary, secondary or optional assignment that starts `assigned` and reaches exactly one terminal state (`succeeded` or `failed`). Tasks OBSERVE T-676 trigger completion via `triggerId`; they never fire `endOn` and they never duplicate objective logic.

READ SINCE T-936.2 by `Objectives/TBD_TaskStateMachine.c` (server-authoritative transitions) and `UI/TBD_TaskHud.c` (one HUD marker per assigned task, hidden once terminal). Absent array ⇒ a mission with no tasks, which is every pre-T-936.2 document; the AUTHORED_BLOCKS carrier emits nothing in that case, so Class-R byte-parity fixtures stay identical.

objectives.description: T-212 / T-685 — typed per-side objective entities (schemaVersion 1.3). Distinct from `zones[]` of `type: objective_*`: a `zone` is a VOLUME with capture RULES, whereas an `objective` is the mission's first-class task record — the container the editor's `objectivesById` compiles into, which today has no mutator and no reader (a dead container, per T-212). Carried on the wire; NOTHING reads it on any shipped build — the Enfusion reader lands under T-212/T-685. Each row is ONE objective with a uniform attribute spine (id/type/side/zoneId/label), optional PER-SIDE `framing` (the attacker/defender readings of the SAME objective — never two rows for one objective; see `$defs/objective`), and WOG's proven capture/defend/height model carried on `zoneRules` (T-685: attackerCount/defenderCount/advantagePercent/minHeight/maxHeight/startingOwner, whose degenerate 1-vs-1 case is a zone's `contestable`). Distinct from `winConditions.endOn` — that is the win TRIGGER vocabulary; this is the objective SUBJECT it fires on.

vehicles.description: T-675 / T-076 — mission-placed VEHICLE roster (schemaVersion 1.3), the compile half split out of T-076 so the crew UI could ship. A vehicle is NOT an `entities[]` alias row: `#/$defs/alias` is `^(kit|comp|veh|preset|layer|prop|item):[a-z0-9_]+$` and the mod's `Data/registry.json` holds exactly ONE `veh:` row, so routing crewed vehicles through `entities[]` would reproduce the T-200 silent-substitution defect with a ten-tonne vehicle (flatten.rs:2631-2640). This is `document root + a new $def`, keyed `vehicles`, carrying seats/crew refs onto the wire. READ SINCE T-675.2 (2026-09-06) by `apps/mod/tbd-framework/Scripts/Game/TBD/Backend/TBD_MissionVehicleStruct.c`, bound through `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct.vehicles` and seated by `TBD_SpawnManager` after the slot bodies materialise. NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE READER: one authored vehicle emits TWO rows — this roster row AND an `entities[]` alias row (flatten.rs:78-83) — and `entities[]` is already spawned by `SpawnMissionEntities()`, so `uid` is the join key the roster reader claims on. Without that claim every crewed vehicle reaches the world twice. Compiled from the editor `vehiclesById` (T-215/T-425), sibling of the payload's own top-level `vehicles` bag but the DECLARED contract shape here.

editorTriggers.description: T-079 / T-676 — editor-authored TRIGGER entities: an activation model (condition/repeat/timeout/owner side) plus an effects model (schemaVersion 1.3). NAMED `editorTriggers`, NOT `triggers`, DELIBERATELY (T-706 forward-constraint 3): `flatten.rs` already emits a win-condition trigger vocabulary as `winConditions.endOn` (values `time_limit` / `faction_eliminated` / …, computed at flatten.rs:2152-2160), and T-079's editor triggers are a DIFFERENT object with a different lifecycle — an authored condition→effect rule, not a round-end predicate. Collapsing them onto one `triggers` key would make a reader unable to tell a win predicate from an authored rule, so they are named apart on the wire; `winConditions.endOn` keeps the win vocabulary and `editorTriggers[]` carries the T-079 runtime. The editor payload rides `triggersById` undeclared today (T-706 forward-constraint 2); this is the compiled, DECLARED shape. READ SINCE T-676 (2026-09-06) by `apps/mod/tbd-framework/Scripts/Game/TBD/Zones/TBD_TriggerRuntime.c`, which takes a SECOND typed `JsonLoadContext` pass over the raw document for this key — `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` declares no field for it, and `JsonLoadContext` binds by member name, so the primary loader structurally cannot see it. Geometry rides the shipped T-582 zone draw tool, so a trigger's area is a `zones[]` row referenced by `zoneId`, not re-declared here.

variants.description: T-654 — the named-variant registry for conditional inclusion (schemaVersion 1.3). Generalises what FNF v3 built by hand with Eden layers: a template ships named modes (`FNF Gamemode: <Mode>`) and the setup script deletes every object/marker belonging to the modes not picked, making the layer name a HARD RUNTIME CONTRACT. Here each variant is declared ONCE by id, and any variant-gated subtree elsewhere in the document (an objective, a vehicle, an entity, a zone, a trigger) references it via `variantId` — the compiler emits that subtree only when the variant is selected. Declaring variants centrally is what lets the `variantId` predicate be validated (an unknown id is catchable) instead of being a free string. NOTHING reads it on any shipped build — the conditional-inclusion compile pass lands under T-654 (which is a DESIGN ticket first; this is the wire shape its design will target).

missionParams.description: T-684 — first-class launch-time mission parameters (schemaVersion 1.3): a mission carries named parameters chosen at LAUNCH rather than baked at authoring time (name, i18n title key, value list, display list, default, consuming symbol). Models Arma's `class Params` — OFCRA runs one artefact as training server, briefing room, mod-check sandbox and match off 29 such entries. READ SINCE T-684 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionParams.c` (both mod trees); launch selection is `$profile:TBD_MissionParams.json` or the authored default. flatten.rs does not yet emit the array onto `/compiled`.

alias.description: Registry alias resolved by the framework registry to a prefab GUID.

cargoContainer.description: Worn container a cargo row is inserted into. CLOSED vocabulary (T-181.34) — unlike kit:/preset: aliases these four are fixed by the ENGINE's worn-garment areas, not by extensible content, so an enum here can never fight the registry. TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.GarmentForContainer maps exactly these to LoadoutVestArea (+ LoadoutArmoredVestSlotArea), LoadoutJacketArea, LoadoutPantsArea and LoadoutBackpackArea, and the Arsenal UI offers exactly these (arsenal_rules.rs CARGO_CONTAINERS). Before this enum a typo validated clean and then DEGRADED at runtime: GarmentForContainer returned null and InsertCargo fell through to TryInsertItem anywhere, so the cargo silently landed in the wrong place instead of failing. armoredVest is deliberately NOT a key — it shares the vest container (single-vest collapse).

wireSafeString.description:
A free-text authored string that reaches a DELIMITED wire, and therefore may not contain a character that FRAMES one. TBD_SpawnManager.BuildSlotRoster, TBD_BriefingData, TBD_LobbyData and TBD_AdminData all serialise to tab-separated fields joined by newlines, so a TAB in an authored value opens a new column and a CR/LF opens a new row. T-181.42 recorded the consequence end to end: a callsign authored `AL<TAB>PHA` was a SCHEMA-VALID mission that produced a seven-field roster row, sailed past the consumer's `< 6` guard, shifted every column, rendered `role` as `PHA`, made the real role read as the STATE (so the seat matched neither OPEN nor DEAD and became UNSELECTABLE), and parsed `holderId` from `"OPEN".ToInt()` = 0. The mod now sanitises at the source (TBD_SpawnManager.RosterField / TBD_BriefingData.Sanitise, both substituting a space and warning once per distinct value) and the lobby parser is pinned to exact arity, so this is DEFENCE IN DEPTH — but the schema is where the class dies, because a rewritten field is still a field the author did not write.

SCOPE — the pattern bans the C0 control block plus DEL, not just the three framing characters. That is a strict superset of \t, \r and \n at zero cost to legitimate authoring (no web-editor author types a control character into a callsign on purpose), it is a CLOSED character class that cannot drift, and it covers the un-sanitised siblings: NUL is a C-string terminator on a byte-indexed engine (`string.Length()` counts BYTES here), and VT/FF are treated as line breaks by enough downstream tooling to be the next hazard. Nothing in the mod strips those three today.

DELIBERATELY NOT BANNED. `.` — the per-field marker (TBD_BriefingData.FIELD_MARK) is BIJECTIVE by construction, `Unmark(Field(x)) == Sanitise(x)` for every x including `.` and the empty string, so an authored dot cannot confuse a reader. `~` — the RETIRED TBD_LobbyData.EMPTY sentinel, replaced precisely because it was lossy; forbidding it would enshrine a convention the tree abandoned. `:` — load-bearing INSIDE slot.id (`{faction}:{groupCallsign}:{role}:{index}`). Zero-width joiners, bidi/RTL overrides and U+2028/U+2029 — a display-SPOOFING class, not a wire-FRAMING one: none of them can shift a column, an open-ended Unicode blocklist is exactly the drifting vocabulary T-181.34 correctly refused to close, and folding two unrelated defects behind one pattern means a failure no longer names its cause. If spoofing is worth gating it deserves its own check and its own negative fixture.

Briefing prose (briefing.situation/mission/execution) is deliberately EXCLUDED from this $ref: it does not ride a delimited wire at all — TBD_BriefingService ships it as parallel `array<string>` RPC parameters, so an embedded newline there is legitimate authoring, not a hazard.

id.description: Content-hash id assigned on publish. Optional in hand-written drafts.

terrain.description: Must match a framework scenario / terrain key.

environment.description:
Mission environment. T-682 adds `fog` / `wind` / `viewDistance` on the WIRE (schemaVersion 1.3) as the scenario-side environment axes (ATTR-FIELD-SCN-FOG / -SCN-WIND / -SCN-VIEW-DIST).

AUTHORING PATH LANDS SEPARATELY — read this before adding an editor control. `env.rs`'s `keys_nothing_reads_are_not_authored` test names `viewDistance` (and `thermals`/`windDirDeg`/`fog`/`wind`) as keys the EDITOR MUST NOT AUTHOR. That frontend test gates AUTHORING, NOT the wire. The mod READER comes first and the control second (`author_env`). READ SINCE T-682 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EnvironmentReader.c` (both mod trees) and `ModEnvironment` serialisation of `fog`/`wind`/`windDirDeg`/`viewDistance` when authored. Editor controls stay refused until a later ticket.

fog.description: T-682 (ATTR-FIELD-SCN-FOG). Fog density, 0 (clear) → 1 (thickest), matching Eden's normalised scenario fog. READ SINCE T-682 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EnvironmentReader.c`.

wind.description: T-682 (ATTR-FIELD-SCN-WIND). Wind STRENGTH (m/s); direction is the existing `windDirDeg`. READ SINCE T-682 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EnvironmentReader.c`.

viewDistance.description: T-682 (ATTR-FIELD-SCN-VIEW-DIST). Terrain/object view distance in metres. READ SINCE T-682 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EnvironmentReader.c`. DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED by the editor (T-193 removed its control; env.rs asserts it stays un-authored). The editor control is a later ticket.

orbat.description: Per-faction order of battle. Keys must match faction keys.

callsign.description: The ORBAT-side CAUSE of slot.groupCallsign. flatten.rs copies this verbatim into slot.groupCallsign and interpolates it into slot.id, and nothing re-validates the compiled document — so constraining only the slot fields would forbid the symptom while permitting the cause.

combatMode.description: T-678 (ATTR-FIELD-GRP-COMBAT-MODE, schemaVersion 1.3). Group rules of engagement, TBD's own ladder blue=never fire → red=open fire, engage at will. These are TBD VOCABULARY mapped onto `EAIGroupCombatMode` (HOLD_FIRE / RETURN_FIRE / FIRE_AT_WILL). READ SINCE T-678 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_GroupState.c`. Applied only when T-677 has already AI-enabled the group.

behaviour.description: T-678 (ATTR-FIELD-GRP-BEHAVIOUR, schemaVersion 1.3). Group behaviour state — TBD vocabulary (careless/safe/aware/combat/stealth). READ SINCE T-677 (2026-09-06) on waypoint overrides via `TBD_WaypointRuntime.c`, and READ SINCE T-678 (2026-09-06) as group defaults via `TBD_GroupState.c`. A waypoint that authors behaviour still wins (WAYPOINT origin).

formation.description: T-678 (ATTR-FIELD-GRP-FORMATION, schemaVersion 1.3). Group movement formation. Enum tokens are the shared vocabulary: T-672's editor `force_to_formation` + Transform submenu consume them (geometry via `formation_offsets`). READ SINCE T-678 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_GroupState.c` (engine four-name set; extras map onto Wedge/Line/Column/StaggeredColumn).

speedMode.description: T-678 (ATTR-FIELD-GRP-SPEED-MODE, schemaVersion 1.3). Group movement speed mode. READ SINCE T-677 (2026-09-06) on waypoint overrides via `TBD_WaypointRuntime.c`, and READ SINCE T-678 (2026-09-06) as group defaults via `TBD_GroupState.c` (DEFAULT origin so a waypoint speedMode still wins).

waypoints.description: T-677 — per-squad waypoint list (schemaVersion 1.3), the nine `ATTR-FIELD-WP-*` ids. READ SINCE T-677 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_WaypointRuntime.c`. `TBD_SpawnManager` opens the AI spawn gate only for waypointed groups. Group combatMode/formation READ SINCE T-678 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_GroupState.c`.

placementRadius.description: T-679 (ATTR-FIELD-GRP-PLACEMENT-RADIUS, schemaVersion 1.3). Metres: the group's members are scattered within this radius of its authored position at spawn (0/absent = exact placement). READ SINCE T-679 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_PlacementScatter.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader. Group scatter is a shared offset because groups have no authored x/z on the wire. The 2D top-down editor is the surface where the scatter circle is drawable.

placementShape.description: T-679 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-SHAPE applied to a group, schemaVersion 1.3). Scatter area shape for `placementRadius`. READ SINCE T-679 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_PlacementScatter.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

variantId.description: T-654 (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this group is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected (conditional inclusion). On the wire only — the variant compile pass lands under T-654.

leaderSlotId.description: T-674 — the TBD-only key naming which slot leads this squad (schemaVersion 1.3). References `slots[].uid` — a durable identity, because `id` is derived and shifts under role renames/reorders/deletes (see the `slot.id` description). This is a PER-SQUAD fact, so it lives here on the wire orbat group (one copy, the T-216 delta table's own proposal) rather than denormalised onto every `slots[]` entry where N copies could disagree with no schema able to catch it — the editor already authors it once per squad at `/editor/squads/*/leaderSlotId`. READ SINCE T-674.2 (2026-09-06) via `TBD_MissionLoader.GetSquadLeaderSlot` / `IsSquadLeader`, which resolve it through the uid-aware slot lookup and then RE-CHECK that the seat belongs to this squad: slot uids are unique document-wide, so a leaderSlotId copied between squads resolves cleanly to a seat in the wrong one and nothing downstream could notice. A cross-squad reference yields no leader rather than a guessed one.

slot.description: The ORBAT-side CAUSE of slot.role — flatten.rs copies it into slot.role and into slot.id. Same reasoning as group.callsign.

radio.description: Net ids this role spawns tuned to.

id.description: Human-readable slot label: {faction}:{groupCallsign}:{role}:{index}. DERIVED each compile — shifts under role renames/reorders/deletes; key durable references on uid instead. Reaches the roster wire as column 1 via slot.Key() when uid is absent.

uid.description: Stable slot identity (B1): the editor document's slot id, carried verbatim so the identity survives recompiles and ORBAT edits. Spawn points, rosters and logs key on this. Optional for pre-B1 documents. (Named uid, not ref — ref is an EnforceScript keyword.) Reaches the roster wire as column 1 — slot.Key() prefers it over id.

y.description: Optional spawn height, metres ASL (schemaVersion 1.2). Maps from the editor's position.z. Absent → the loader uses terrain surface Y.

loadout.description: Optional per-slot Arsenal loadout (T-068.11), flattened from the editor SlotLoadoutV2. Additive data: JsonLoadContext readers ignore unknown keys, so this ships WITHOUT a schemaVersion bump (the mod loader allowlists 1.1/1.2); T-068.12 reads it to equip the human player. The kit alias stays authoritative for the base character — loadout layers on top.

gear.description: Fixed gear ResourceNames. WEAR derivation: jacket→uniform, armoredVest else vest→vest (single-vest collapse, documented), headCover→helmet; pants/boots/handwear/backpack copied verbatim since A3. WEAPONS (T-182): all FOUR editor weapon slots are carried, each selected by the exact (slotIndex, slotType) pair the Arsenal authors — (0,primary)→primary, (1,primary)→launcher, (2,secondary)→handgun, (3,grenade)→throwable — and each keeps the editor's own key name so the compiled document reads the same words the Arsenal UI shows (arsenal_rules.rs WEAPON_SLOTS is the source of that mapping). optic/magazine ride the (0,primary) rifle ALONE; the other three weapons carry no sub-slots today. Before T-182 the compiler selected ONLY (0,primary) and silently discarded launcher/handgun/throwable — this prose used to describe that partial mapping as complete, which is why the loss shipped unnoticed. Empty slots are omitted, never empty strings. T-310: optional attachments[] (wireSafeString ResourceNames) from the (0,primary) SlotLoadoutV2 edges; omitted when empty.

attachments.description: T-310. Optional. Primary-rifle Arsenal attachment ResourceNames, copied from SlotLoadoutV2 weapons[].attachments edges on (slotIndex 0, slotType primary). Omitted when empty. Mounted by TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper after optic/magazine.

cargo.description: Container cargo rows ({container,item,qty} — the loadout-export v2 shape), copied verbatim from the editor cargo (T-068.15.2). Omitted when empty.

callsign.description: T-674 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-CALLSIGN, schemaVersion 1.3). A per-slot display callsign, distinct from `groupCallsign` (the ORBAT group name) and from `id` (the derived label). READ SINCE T-674.2 (2026-09-06): bound on `TBD_MissionSlotStruct` and logged per identified seat. Reforger exposes NO replicated free-text name on a character (`CharacterIdentityComponent.SetIdentityFromIDs` takes indices into a faction identity table), so this reaches every surface holding the slot and the server log, and is deliberately NOT pushed onto the spawned entity. `wireSafeString`-constrained because it reaches the same tab-delimited roster wire as `id`.

rank.description: T-674 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-RANK, schemaVersion 1.3). Character rank — TBD's own ladder (private → colonel); READ SINCE T-674.2 (2026-09-06). The engine type is `SCR_ECharacterRank` with unprefixed members PRIVATE/CORPORAL/SERGEANT/LIEUTENANT/CAPTAIN/MAJOR/COLONEL (also RENEGADE and GENERAL, which TBD does not author), applied through `SCR_CharacterRankComponent.SetCharacterRank` and replicated. TBD's ladder is an exact lowercase subset. The names here remain the contract; a kit prefab with no rank component is reported at WARNING rather than silently dropping the authored rank.

stance.description: T-674 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-STANCE, schemaVersion 1.3). Initial spawn pose. READ SINCE T-674.2 (2026-09-06), applied through `CharacterControllerComponent.SetStanceChange` on EVERY spawn including respawn, because a fresh body inherits nothing.

unitName.description: T-674 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-UNIT-NAME, schemaVersion 1.3). A per-slot unit name that rides this slice rather than standing alone (the sweep says so explicitly). READ SINCE T-674.2 (2026-09-06): bound on the slot and logged, not pushed onto the entity, for the same reason as `callsign` — read that description. `wireSafeString`-constrained (reaches a delimited wire).

tag.description: T-674 — the TBD-only slot tag key (schemaVersion 1.3), mirroring the ORBAT-slot `tag` the events path already carries (T-010). READ SINCE T-674.2 (2026-09-06): bound on the slot and logged. Like `callsign` and `unitName` it has no engine target that reaches a client, so it is not pushed onto the spawned entity.

placementRadius.description: T-679 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-PLACEMENT-RADIUS, schemaVersion 1.3). Metres: this slot is scattered within this radius of its authored (x, z) at spawn (0/absent = exact). READ SINCE T-679 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_PlacementScatter.c` (`ForSlot` from SpawnSlotBody). Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

placementShape.description: T-679 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-SHAPE, schemaVersion 1.3). Scatter area shape for this slot's `placementRadius`. READ SINCE T-679 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_PlacementScatter.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

gadgets.description: T-705 (schemaVersion 1.3). Which personal gadgets this player spawns with (map/compass/watch/gps/radio), the Eden General-States model that lets a scenario decide a player's gadgets. On the wire only — every flag needs an Enfusion reader in apps/mod/tbd-framework, none of which exists on any shipped build; the readers land under T-705 (this is the schema half, split out of T-705 for the one-pass widening).

variantId.description: T-654 (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this slot is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. On the wire only — lands under T-654.

radioPlan.description: Shared contract consumed by the framework and the partner VOIP bridge. Nets map to voice channels.

nets.description: T-275: `maxItems` 32 pins `TBD_RadioPlan.MAX_NETS` (TBD_RadioPlan.c:91). The mod truncates to the first 32 valid nets and warns — without this, a document can validate and still drop authored channels.

label.description: T-275: `maxLength` 48 pins `TBD_RadioPlan.MAX_LABEL_CHARS` (TBD_RadioPlan.c:94). The mod truncates over-long labels via CapLabel — without this, a document can validate and still show a shortened channel name.

range.description: T-292: which radio class this net prefers. Enfusion exposes exactly two gadget types — EGadgetType.RADIO (handheld) and EGadgetType.RADIO_BACKPACK — and the mod wire is a 0/1 flag (TBD_RadioService.LongRangeFlag → m_aLongRange). short → handheld (flag 0); long → backpack (flag 1). There is no third hardware class, so the retired value any is rejected here rather than kept as a synonym that looked distinct while collapsing to the same flag as short.

shape.description: Exactly one of circle or polygon.

markerArea.description: T-673 (schemaVersion 1.3). The extent of an AREA marker — a SUPERSET of `#/$defs/shape` (circle | polygon) that ALSO expresses the rectangle and ellipse extents Eden's second marker model needs, which `#/$defs/shape` cannot (a rect/ellipse has a centre, half-extents and a rotation, not a radius or a ring). Exactly one of circle / polygon / rectangle / ellipse. This def, not `shape` (the icon-glyph selector on `marker`), is the AUTHORITATIVE geometry of an area marker: when a `marker.area` is present the marker IS an area marker and `marker.shape` is ignored (precedence stated on both). On the wire only — the area-marker reader lands under T-673.

rectExtent.description: T-673 (schemaVersion 1.3). The extent of a rectangle or ellipse area marker: a centre `(x, z)`, half-extents `halfWidth`/`halfHeight` (metres, so the full box is 2·halfWidth by 2·halfHeight), and a `rotationDeg`. Shared by the `rectangle` and `ellipse` arms of `#/$defs/markerArea` — an ellipse is the same bounding box read as an oval, matching Eden's rectangular/elliptical marker areas.

label.description: Optional human name. Reaches the briefing Z record via TBD_BriefingService.PrettyZoneTitle, which falls back to type + zone.id when this is empty — so both keys are on that wire. No minLength: an empty label is a committed golden (empty-warning-fields.json) and means "use the fallback".

variantId.description: T-654 (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this zone is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. On the wire only — lands under T-654.

zoneRules.description:
Zone-type specific rules. OPTIONAL as a whole — a zone that authors no `rules` runs entirely on the defaults named per key below.

WHY THIS IS A CLOSED VOCABULARY (T-241). Both readers are TYPED: Enfusion's `JsonLoadContext` maps JSON keys onto named class fields, so a key the class does not declare is INVISIBLE to it — not rejected, not logged, simply absent. `TBD_ZoneRegistry.ResolveRules` then reports "no rule this build understands was readable", which is true of both "authored nothing" and "authored `graceSecconds`", and a typed parser cannot tell those apart. That makes this schema the ONLY place a misspelled rule key can be caught, so `additionalProperties` is false and every key the mod reads is declared here. Adding a rule to the vocabulary is a field in the reader plus a property here.

WHY THE VOCABULARY IS FLAT AND NOT NARROWED BY `zone.type`. Neither reader is type-conditional. `TBD_MissionZoneRulesStruct` (TBD_MissionLoader.c:93-105) is parsed for every zone and `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` (TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:76-101) runs a second pass over every zone in the same document, so `captureSeconds` on a boundary zone parses and is ignored exactly as it is today. Narrowing per type here would declare a rule the runtime does not enforce; the per-key descriptions name the consuming zone type instead. `TBD_ZoneRegistry.ResolveRules` only SUPPRESSES its diagnostics for types it does not enforce (`report`), it does not reject the keys.

WHY THERE ARE MINIMA AND MAXIMA. Each minimum below is the reader's own error branch (`< 0` or `<= 0`), where an out-of-range value is discarded in favour of the default. Each maximum pins the matching mod sanity CEILING (T-275): `graceSeconds` ≤ `TBD_ZoneRegistry.MAX_GRACE_SECONDS` (3600); `captureSeconds` / `neutralizeSeconds` / `holdSeconds` ≤ `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` (21600). Those ceilings used to be runtime-only (warn + fall back / inert); encoding them here means a document cannot validate and still be clamped.

PRESENCE. Numeric and string keys carry an ABSENT sentinel (-1e6; -1 for the one integer, because `targetCount: 0` is meaningful) so a bad authored value is reported as an error instead of being mistaken for "not authored". BOOLS CANNOT — there is no third value — so for the four booleans "absent" and "authored false" are indistinguishable at runtime and always will be. Each bool's default is the value an author gets by writing nothing, so nothing is lost behaviourally.

graceSeconds.description: PLAY AREA (`boundary`, `base_protection`). Seconds a player may remain in violation before `penalty` is applied. Read at TBD_MissionLoader.c:102, resolved at TBD_ZoneRegistry.c:387-397. Negative is rejected for the default. T-275: `maximum` 3600 pins `TBD_ZoneRegistry.MAX_GRACE_SECONDS` (TBD_ZoneRegistry.c:52) — above that the mod warns and falls back to 30 s.

warnEverySeconds.description: PLAY AREA (`boundary`, `base_protection`). How often, in seconds, a player in violation is told. Read at TBD_MissionLoader.c:103, resolved at TBD_ZoneRegistry.c:401-413. Zero would mean "warn every frame", so the reader requires > 0.

penalty.description: PLAY AREA (`boundary`, `base_protection`). What happens once `graceSeconds` elapses. `none` tracks server-side and says nothing; `warn` tells the player and never acts; `kill` is TERMINAL under one life. Read at TBD_MissionLoader.c:104, matched against TBD_ZoneRegistry.PENALTY_* at :419-438 (enum TBD_EZonePenalty, TBD_Zone.c:36-41). A value outside this set resolves to `warn`, never `kill` — the mod refuses to guess toward ending a player's only life, and this enum is what stops a typo getting that far.

captureSeconds.description: `objective_capture`. Seconds of uninterrupted presence needed to take a NEUTRAL objective. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:85, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:441-457. Absent DEFAULTS rather than going inert: an objective nobody chose the length of is playable, whereas an inert one takes the `all_objectives_captured` trigger with it and the round can no longer be won. T-275: `maximum` 21600 pins `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` (TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:60).

neutralizeSeconds.description: `objective_capture`. Seconds of presence needed to tear a HELD objective back to neutral. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:86, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:462-472. Defaults to `captureSeconds` (a symmetric 1:1 rate), so there is no literal default to state here. `0` is legal and means instant — a single-stage capture. T-275: `maximum` 21600 pins `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` (TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:60).

contestable.description: `objective_capture`. Does an enemy inside stop the capture? True freezes progress while two sides are present; false resolves by weight of numbers and freezes only on an exact tie. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:97, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:476; meaning fixed at TBD_Objective.c:262-299.

onEmpty.description: `objective_capture`. What happens to partial progress when NOBODY is inside. `hold` keeps it; `decay` bleeds it back at `decayRate`. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:95, matched against TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.ON_EMPTY_* at :478-492. An unrecognised value resolves to `hold`.

decayRate.description: `objective_capture`, and only meaningful with `onEmpty: "decay"`. Progress-seconds lost per real second while decaying — `1` bleeds at the rate it was earned. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:88, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:495-506.

holdSeconds.description: `objective_hold_until`, and EFFECTIVELY REQUIRED there. Seconds the zone's `faction` must hold the ground. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:87, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:539-550. There is deliberately NO default: a hold is the length of the round (`last-stand-at-montfort.json` authors 2700 s inside a 3000 s limit), so guessing it means guessing when the round ends and who won. An objective_hold_until with no readable `holdSeconds` goes INERT and reports why. Not declared `required` here because the readers do not reject the document — see the $def description on why this vocabulary is not narrowed by zone type. T-275: `maximum` 21600 pins `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` (TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:60) — above that the mod marks the objective inert.

pauseOnEnemy.description: `objective_hold_until`. An enemy inside PAUSES the hold clock. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:98, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:553.

resetOnEnemy.description: `objective_hold_until`. An enemy inside RESETS the hold clock to zero. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:99, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:554.

requireHolderPresent.description: `objective_hold_until`. The hold clock only runs while a friendly is inside. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:100, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:555.

targetAlias.description: `objective_destroy`, and EFFECTIVELY REQUIRED there. Registry alias of the thing that must be destroyed (e.g. "comp:ammo_cache"). Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:94, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.ArmDestroyTargets; an objective_destroy with no readable alias goes INERT because there is nothing to watch. Constrained to the same `#/$defs/alias` form as `entity.alias` — it is resolved through the same framework registry. T-254: `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` models `entities[]` and `SpawnMissionEntities` places resolvable rows after parse; ArmDestroyTargets then AABB-queries the zone. INERT reasons distinguish unresolved registry alias vs no matching `entities[]` row vs out-of-zone authorship vs spawn/query miss (T-437) — never a 'build does not spawn entities[]' claim.

targetCount.description: `objective_destroy`. How many matching targets must die. `0` (or absent) means ALL of them, which is why the reader's absent-sentinel for this key is -1 rather than 0. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:92, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:577-588.

points.description: EVERY objective type. Score carried and reported on completion. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:90, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:399-410. No default is stated because no end trigger in this build consumes it — it is transported, not scored.

announceEverySeconds.description: EVERY objective type. How often a player standing on the objective is told the progress. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:89, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:412-423. No single default is stated because the default is per zone type: 15 s for `objective_capture` (DEFAULT_CAPTURE_ANNOUNCE_SECONDS) and 60 s for `objective_hold_until` (DEFAULT_HOLD_ANNOUNCE_SECONDS).

attackerCount.description: T-685 (schemaVersion 1.3). `objective_capture`. How many attackers must be inside to make progress — WOG's `_CaptureCount` (observed 4x128 / 1x16 / 2x6 / 3x5 across 166 instances). TBD's `contestable: bool` is the degenerate 1-vs-1 case of this + `defenderCount`. READ SINCE T-685 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_ZoneVolume.c` / `TBD_MissionZoneRulesStruct` bind / `TBD_ObjectivesComponent.c` apply. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader. Absent ⇒ 1; authored 0 turns the count gate off.

defenderCount.description: T-685 (schemaVersion 1.3). `objective_capture` / `objective_hold_until`. How many defenders must be inside to HOLD — WOG's `_DefCount` (observed 3x129 / 1x17 / 2x8 / 0x5). READ SINCE T-685 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_ZoneVolume.c` / loader bind / `TBD_ObjectivesComponent.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

advantagePercent.description: T-685 (schemaVersion 1.3). `objective_capture`. The numeric advantage (percent) one side needs before capture progresses — WOG's `_AdvantagePercent` (observed 2x72 / 0x67 / 4x14 / 3x13). READ SINCE T-685 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_ZoneVolume.c` / loader bind / `TBD_ObjectivesComponent.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

minHeight.description: T-685 (schemaVersion 1.3). The objective volume's LOWER bound, metres ABOVE TERRAIN (AGL), evaluated at each tested ENTITY's own ground position — not ASL, and not anchored to the zone centre. AXIS + EVALUATION POINT stated because a slope makes the two readings diverge by tens of metres, which is precisely the behaviour these bounds exist for: a small negative min (WOG's `_MinHeight` = -5 INVARIANT across all 166 instances) reaches basements-in under the entity, while a bounded max excludes aircraft overhead — both judged per-entity, so a POLYGON zone needs no separate height anchor (each entity supplies its own terrain reference). Together with `maxHeight` this makes an objective a 3D VOLUME rather than a flat footprint. READ SINCE T-685 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_ZoneVolume.c` (AGL at each entity's own ground). Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

maxHeight.description: T-685 (schemaVersion 1.3). The objective volume's UPPER bound, metres ABOVE TERRAIN (AGL), evaluated at each tested ENTITY's own ground position (same axis and evaluation point as `minHeight` — AGL per-entity, not ASL, not anchored to the zone centre; WOG's `_MaxHeight`, observed 30x137 / 15x16 / 20x13, is read as excluding aircraft). READ SINCE T-685 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_ZoneVolume.c` / loader bind / `TBD_ObjectivesComponent.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

startingOwner.description: T-685 (schemaVersion 1.3). Which faction holds this objective at round start — WOG's `_Owner` (observed 1x70 / 0x65 / 2x30 / 4x1). Constrained to `factionKey` — it names a `factions[].key`. READ SINCE T-685 (2026-09-07) by `TBD_ZoneVolume.c` / loader bind / `TBD_ObjectivesComponent.c`. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

vehicleClasses.description: T-689 (schemaVersion 1.3). PLAY AREA (`boundary`, `base_protection`). WHICH VEHICLE CLASSES the play-area rule applies to — the missing axis on TBD's otherwise-complete play-area model (graceSeconds/warnEverySeconds/penalty). FNF v4 documents exactly why it exists: the play-zone group's air flag is `false` so AIRCRAFT MAY LEAVE the play area while ground vehicles and infantry may not (`fn_addRestrictionGroup.sqf`). PRESENCE SEMANTICS (there is no `minItems`, so all three cases are legal and defined here): ABSENT means the rule applies to EVERYTHING — every vehicle class and infantry are confined (today's behaviour); a NON-EMPTY list restricts the rule to exactly the classes named, so omitting `aircraft` from the list is how the aircraft exemption is authored; an EMPTY list `[]` is the explicit INVERSE of absent — the rule applies to NO vehicle class, so nothing is confined by it (no vehicle is disallowed from leaving). `[]` therefore is NOT the same as absent, and this clause is what defines it. On the wire only — no reader on any shipped build; the class-filtered enforcement lands under T-689.

entity.description: One mission-placed world object. Read the top-level `entities` description before building on this — nothing on any shipped build spawns one.

uid.description: T-946.18 (schemaVersion 1.3) — stable identity for this entity, carried verbatim from the editor, the same role `slot.uid` and `vehicle.uid` play. THIS IS THE JOIN KEY BETWEEN THE TWO ROWS ONE AUTHORED VEHICLE EMITS: T-675.1 emits a placed vehicle as an `entities[]` alias row AND a `vehicles[]` roster row, deliberately, and until this property existed the two had nothing in common to match on — while the mod already spawns `entities[]` (`TBD_MissionLoader.SpawnMissionEntities`), so a roster reader would have spawned every crewed vehicle twice. A reader dedupes on `entity.uid == vehicle.uid`. Optional: an entity nothing references needs no uid, and a blank or wire-unsafe authored id yields no key rather than a repaired one.

health.description: T-681 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-HEALTH, schemaVersion 1.3). Initial health fraction, 0 (destroyed) → 1 (pristine). READ SINCE T-681 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EntityState.c` (`DamageManagerComponent.SetHealthScaled`) on spawned `entities[]` bodies. Unset leaves the prefab default. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36); hand-staged 1.3 JSON reaches the reader.

READ SINCE T-681 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EntityState.c` (`EnableDamageHandling(true)`) only when bound true. Authored false and omit bind identically (T-946.37 class). Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36).

READ SINCE T-681 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EntityState.c` (`SetFlags(VISIBLE)`) only when bound true. Authored false (hide) cannot be distinguished from omit. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36).

size.description: T-681 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-SIZE, schemaVersion 1.3). Uniform scale multiplier for the placed object (1 = native size). READ SINCE T-681 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_EntityState.c` (`IEntity.SetScale`). Unset leaves the prefab scale. Identifier count collides with T-673 marker.size (UNREAD re-pin, not retire). Flatten still omits the entity key on `/compiled` (T-946.36).

stamina.description: T-681 (ATTR-FIELD-OBJ-STAMINA, schemaVersion 1.3). Whether stamina is enabled for a character entity. READ SINCE T-681 (2026-09-06) as a bound identifier on `TBD_EntityState.c`; Reforger exposes no per-character stamina enable toggle (`BaseStaminaComponent.GetStamina` only), so authored true is logged and skipped. Flatten still omits the key on `/compiled` (T-946.36).

variantId.description: T-654 (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this entity is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. On the wire only — lands under T-654.

entityInventory.description:
What an author puts INTO this entity's own storage — the vehicle/crate answer to the question `slot.loadout.cargo` answers for a worn garment (T-198).

WHY THIS IS NOT A cargoContainer ROW. `#/$defs/cargoContainer` is [vest, pants, jacket, backpack] and is closed by the ENGINE's worn-garment areas, not by content: TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.GarmentForContainer resolves each key to a LoadoutArea on a CHARACTER, and the negative golden cargo-container-typo.json exists to keep it closed. Widening it to admit `vehicle`/`crate` was proposed and DECLINED — a vehicle is not a garment, and an enum that means "worn area" cannot be made to also mean "any object with storage" without losing the property that made it safe to close. Here the CONTAINER IS THE ENTITY, which is why these rows carry no `container` key at all: there is exactly one storage to address and `alias` already names it. Nor is a sub-compartment vocabulary invented — naming vehicle bays would be exactly the extensible-content enum T-181.34 correctly refused to close.

NO CAPACITY FIELDS, deliberately. The limits already exist per prefab in registry-items.schema.json — `max_weight_kg` / `max_volume_cm3` / `cargo_grid_w` / `cargo_grid_h` (T-068.15.1) — across 218 `vehicle` and 311 `crate` rows, and the join is live today: entity.alias -> registry.json entry.guid -> the registry-items row keyed by that same ResourceName. `veh:m151_mg` resolves to {F6B23D17D5067C11}Prefabs/Vehicles/Wheeled/M151A2/M151A2_M2HB.et = 360 kg / 25000 cm3 / a 4x125 grid. Restating any of that here would be a SECOND source of truth for a number the mission does not own, and the copy would go stale the first time the prefab is rebalanced. The mission says WHAT goes in; the registry says HOW MUCH fits.

ADDITIVE, never a wipe. A row is INSERTED into whatever the prefab already spawns carrying — the same layering `slot.loadout` does over the kit alias. Absent and `[]` therefore mean the SAME thing: leave the prefab's own contents alone. An "empty it first" semantic would need its own key and must never be spelled as the ABSENCE of this one, because that would silently redefine every mission authored before this key existed.

NO CONSUMER YET — see the top-level `entities` description. This defines the contract; it does not deliver the capability.

item.description: Enfusion ResourceName of the prefab to insert. Same vocabulary as `slot.loadout.cargo[].item` on purpose — ONE item spelling per document, so a given rifle is not a registry alias when it sits in a crate and a ResourceName when it sits in a vest.

qty.description: UNIT COUNT, not a stack size. The character-side reader this mirrors (TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.InsertCargo) spawns the prefab once per unit and inserts each one separately; an entity-side reader has the same engine primitive available against the entity's storage (SCR_InventoryStorageManagerComponent.TryInsertItemInStorage).

objective.description:
T-212 / T-685 — one typed objective entity (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the top-level `objectives` description first: NOTHING reads this on any shipped build; the Enfusion reader lands under T-212. Carries the UNIFORM ATTRIBUTE SPINE every objective shares (id/type/side/zoneId/label) plus the T-212-decided fields below. The `type` is the SUBJECT vocabulary (what kind of task), distinct from `winConditions.endOn`'s TRIGGER vocabulary (when the round ends) and from `zone.type`'s VOLUME-with-rules. Capture-tuning numbers (attackerCount/defenderCount/advantagePercent/min/maxHeight/startingOwner) live on `zoneRules` where the runtime already reads them; this def carries the objective's IDENTITY, not a second copy of those numbers.

ONE ENTITY, TWO FRAMINGS — NOT TWO ROWS. T-212's decision from FNF v4: an objective reads differently to attacker and defender (different task text and titles, separate My Tasks / Ally Tasks trees), but that is ONE objective with per-side FRAMING, authored via the optional `framing` object below. The two-modules-per-objective shape v4 shipped is explicitly FORBIDDEN here — a document must NOT carry two `objectives[]` rows that are 'the same objective' for opposite sides (v4's four documented defects: positional identity, two modules only linked by a shared prefix/target, nothing validating both halves exist, and a lobby tool dividing objective counts by 2 so a forgotten second half yields a fractional count). TBD's stable `uid`/derived `id` already makes v4's positional-identity defect unreachable; do not regress it by splitting an objective across rows.

DROPPED (T-212 correction): the earlier `callsign`/`rank`/`stance` fields had NO source — they were slot-identity copy-through, not part of WOG's `WMT_Task_Point` spine (the best-evidenced objective design in the corpus, 166 instances × 15 parameters), and are removed. The capture/defend/height parameters WOG proved live on `zoneRules` (T-685).

type.description: The task kind. Named apart from `zone.type` (which is the enforcement volume) and `winConditions.endOn` (the round-end predicate). `defend` is a FRAMING of the same objective a `capture` presents to the other side — it does NOT license a second row for the opposing side (see the def description: one entity, two framings).

side.description: Which faction primarily owns / must complete this objective (a `factions[].key`). The other side's reading is authored via `framing`, not a separate objective row.

zoneId.description: The `zones[].id` that gives this objective its geometry and capture rules — an objective points at its enforcement volume rather than restating the shape, so the T-582-drawn zone is the single source of the footprint.

label.description: The objective's neutral display name. Per-side task text/titles are authored in `framing`; this is the side-agnostic label.

framing.description: T-212 — the PER-SIDE FRAMING of this one objective (FNF v4's real insight, implemented as one entity rather than two modules). Optional; when absent the objective reads the same to everyone off `label`/`type`. Each side gets its own task title and text — 'Seize the hilltop' to the attacker, 'Hold the hilltop' to the defender — from a SINGLE objective, so there is never a second row to keep in sync. On the wire only — the reader lands under T-212.

lock.description: T-212 — WOG's `_Lock` (observed 1 in 136 of 166 `Task_Point` instances). Whether this objective is locked at round start. SEMANTICS ARE INFERRED — `wmt_main` is absent from the WOG corpus, so the parameter NAME and observed VALUE are hard evidence but the reading of what a locked objective does is inference and must not be treated as fact by the reader. On the wire only — lands under T-212.

autoLose.description: T-212 — WOG's `_AutoLose` (wog.md:400 distribution: -1 (disabled) x156, live side-1 x10 — 166 carried it). When set, names the `factions[].key` that automatically LOSES if this objective falls; absent/disabled dominates but ten instances used it live, which is why the field is carried. SEMANTICS ARE INFERRED (see `lock` — `wmt_main` is not in the corpus), so this is carried as declared vocabulary, not asserted behaviour. On the wire only — lands under T-212.

variantId.description: T-654. When set, this objective is emitted only if the named variant is selected.

objectiveFraming.description: T-212 — one side's reading of an objective: its task title and body text, shown in that side's task tree. Both optional so a side may frame only a title or only text.

vehicle.description: T-675 / T-076 — one mission-placed vehicle (schemaVersion 1.3). `alias` is the `veh:` (or comp:) registry alias; `seats` carries the crew plan (which slots ride where) so the crew UI's authored state reaches the game. Crew spawn READ SINCE T-675.2. `lock`/`fuel`/`ammo` READ SINCE T-680 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_VehicleState.c`. A FIRST-CLASS row, not an alias-substituted `entities[]` entry.

uid.description: T-675 — stable identity for this roster vehicle (schemaVersion 1.3), carried verbatim from the editor so a reference survives recompiles and edits — the same role `slot.uid` plays for a slot. A `get_in` waypoint's `vehicleUid` names this. Optional; a vehicle nothing references needs no uid. READ SINCE T-675.2 (2026-09-06): it is the JOIN KEY the roster reader claims on, because one authored vehicle emits both this row and an `entities[]` alias row carrying the same uid, and only the claim stops the vehicle being spawned twice. A roster row with no uid falls back to an `alias|x|z` fingerprint.

seats.description: Crew assignment plan: which slot fills which crew position. `slotId` references `slots[].uid` — the durable identity, not the derived `id` (see the `slot.id` description on why references key on uid). `role` is the crew position. The `seats/crew refs` T-076's crew UI authors.

index.description: Disambiguates multiple positions of the same `role` (e.g. cargo seat 0, 1, 2…).

lock.description: T-680 lock state on the roster vehicle (schemaVersion 1.3). READ SINCE T-680 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_VehicleState.c` (`LockPilotControls`; authored true only, bool cannot distinguish omit from false).

variantId.description: T-654. When set, this vehicle is emitted only if the named variant is selected.

editorTrigger.description: T-079 / T-676 — one editor-authored trigger (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the top-level `editorTriggers` description first (including WHY it is not named `triggers`): read since T-676 by `TBD_TriggerRuntime.c`. An `activation` model (condition/repeat/timeout/owner side) fires an `effects` model. Geometry is a `zones[]` reference (`zoneId`), riding the shipped T-582 zone draw tool rather than re-declaring a shape here — the twelve `ATTR-FIELD-TRG-*` ids this ticket owns are activation + effects; the geometry/palette half is elsewhere.

zoneId.description: The `zones[].id` whose volume arms this trigger (T-582 draw tool). A trigger without a zone is a document-wide condition.

condition.description: What makes the trigger fire. Modelled on Eden's activation types; the closest existing TBD semantics are `$defs/zoneRules` (16 keys, the nearest thing TBD has to trigger semantics — read them before the reader lands).

ownerSide.description: Which faction's presence/detection the condition tests.

repeat.description: Whether the trigger re-arms after firing (Eden's repeatable flag).

timeoutSeconds.description: Delay between the condition holding and the effects firing.

effects.description: What happens when `activation` fires — an ordered list of effect records. `type` is the effect kind; `params` is an open bag the reader interprets (the effects vocabulary is a NEW Enfusion runtime, so its shape is deliberately not frozen into a closed enum here beyond the coarse `type`).

params.description: Effect-specific parameters, interpreted by the T-676 reader. Open by design — see the def description.

variantId.description: T-654. When set, this trigger is emitted only if the named variant is selected.

variant.description: T-654 — one named variant in the conditional-inclusion registry (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the top-level `variants` description first: NOTHING reads this on any shipped build. Declaring a variant here by `id` is what makes a `variantId` reference elsewhere validatable (an unknown id is a catchable error rather than a silent free string), which is the whole point of a central registry — it turns FNF v3's by-hand `FNF Gamemode: <Mode>` layer-name convention into a checked contract.

id.description: Stable variant key, referenced by every subtree's `variantId`.

default.description: Whether this variant is selected when the launcher makes no choice.

variantIdRef.description: T-654 — a reference to a `variants[].id`. Same shape as `variant.id` so a subtree's `variantId` and the registry entry it points at cannot disagree on form. WHOLE-DOCUMENT referential integrity (every `variantId` names a declared variant) is a graph check the T-654 reader owns, not something JSON Schema draft 2020-12 can express here — the pattern pins the SHAPE, the same split `entity.alias` uses (schema shape here, registry existence in the gate).

missionParam.description: T-684 — one launch-time mission parameter (schemaVersion 1.3). READ SINCE T-684 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionParams.c`. Models Arma's `class Params` row: a named value chosen at launch, with a title key for i18n, the list of allowed values and their display strings, a default, and the symbol the mission consumes it through.

titleKey.description: i18n key for the launcher-facing title.

displays.description: Parallel display strings for `values` (Arma's `texts[]`). When present, must line up 1:1 with `values` — a length check the T-684 reader owns.

default.description: The value used when the launcher makes no choice (must be one of `values` — a membership check the T-684 reader owns).

waypoint.description: T-677 — one squad waypoint (schemaVersion 1.3). READ SINCE T-677 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_WaypointRuntime.c` (both mod trees). Ordered by position in the array; `type` is the waypoint kind, `x`/`z` its position. The AI spawn gate opens only for waypointed groups.

type.description: Waypoint kind — TBD vocabulary the reader maps onto whatever engine waypoint types Reforger exposes; the names here are the contract, not an engine identifier (no `SCR_AIWaypoint`-style family is asserted — verify the real engine types when the reader lands).

y.description: Optional waypoint height, metres ASL (same policy as `slot.y`).

vehicleUid.description: T-677 (schemaVersion 1.3). For a `get_in` (and, when boarding a specific vehicle, `get_out`) waypoint: the target vehicle, referenced by a `vehicles[].uid`-style stable id, so the squad boards THE authored vehicle rather than any nearby one by proximity inference. Absent → proximity/nearest, the only behaviour available before this key. Ignored for non-boarding waypoint types. READ SINCE T-677 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_WaypointRuntime.c`.

behaviour.description: Per-waypoint behaviour override (falls back to the group's `behaviour`).

speedMode.description: Per-waypoint speed override (falls back to the group's `speedMode`).

gadgetFlags.description: T-705 — per-player gadget presence flags (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the `slot.gadgets` description first: NOTHING reads these on any shipped build. Each is Eden's General-States gadget toggle; ABSENT means "leave the kit's default", `true`/`false` force the gadget on/off. Every flag needs its own Enfusion reader in apps/mod/tbd-framework (the T-705 half); a bool cannot express "absent vs authored false" at runtime, but the kit default covers the absent case, so nothing is lost behaviourally.

map.description: T-705 — spawn with a map. On the wire only; reader lands under T-705.

compass.description: T-705 — spawn with a compass. On the wire only; reader lands under T-705.

watch.description: T-705 — spawn with a watch. On the wire only; reader lands under T-705.

gps.description: T-705 — spawn with a GPS. On the wire only; reader lands under T-705.

radio.description: T-705 — spawn with a personal radio. On the wire only; reader lands under T-705.

winConditions.description:
How the round is won (T-936.1).

`endOn` is the CLOSED list of triggers that may END the round and is unchanged by T-936.1 — `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.EvaluateEndTriggers` drives three of them and `TBD_FrameworkManager.TickWinConditions` the other two. `mode` is the AUTHORED WIN RULE that sits on top of them, and until T-936.1 it was a free `minLength: 1` string that `flatten.rs` hardcoded to `attrition` no matter what the author chose — so it could not be wrong and it could not be right either.

═══ WHY THE ENUM CARRIES SEVEN VALUES AND NOT FIVE ═══

The five the editor authors are `attrition` | `objective` | `extraction` | `vip` | `timeout` (`crates/map-engine-core/src/mission/win_conditions.rs` `AUTHORED_MODES`, and the `mode` enum in `mission-editor-payload.schema.json`, which lists ONLY those five — an editor payload cannot carry the other two).

`points_then_attrition` and `defender_holds_or_attacker_destroys` are GRANDFATHERED. They are not editor output and no slice will ever emit them: they are carried by four committed hand-authored goldens (`bridgehead-at-levie`, `empty-warning-fields`, `slot-loadout-coverage`, `last-stand-at-montfort`) plus two `golden-missions-invalid` fixtures, all of which pre-date the enum and must keep validating — this ticket's own acceptance says so. Dropping them would fail `xtask schema validate` on six committed files whose subject is the mod's PARSER, not the win rule.

They cost nothing at runtime. `mode` reaches the mod at exactly one place — `TBD_BriefingData.BuildWinConditions` renders `Humanise(mode)` on the briefing screen — and `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator` treats any mode outside the five as MODE_UNKNOWN, which is the pre-T-936.1 behaviour those documents were written for: the round ends on `endOn` alone.

═══ PER-MODE PARAMS ═══

`extractionZoneId` / `vipSlotId` / `timeoutMinutes` are each REQUIRED BY, and only meaningful to, one mode — the `allOf` below states that per mode rather than leaving three optional keys nothing has to fill in. `win_conditions.rs` additionally REFUSES a param that belongs to a different mode than the one authored, which a schema `if/then` could express only as a fourth pile of conditionals; the compile is the authoring gate and says which param and which mode.

mode.description: The authored win rule. Five editor-authorable values plus two grandfathered golden-only values — see this block's own note for why the enum is seven wide. `attrition` is what `flatten.rs` emits when the payload authors no `winConditions` at all, which is what keeps every pre-T-936.1 mission byte-identical.

extractionZoneId.description:
The `zones[].id` an extracting side must reach. REQUIRED by `mode: extraction`; OPTIONAL on `mode: vip`, where it is what makes "the VIP got out" a thing the game can observe — without a zone, a VIP rule can only ever end on the VIP's death, which is half a rule. No other mode may carry it (`win_conditions.rs` refuses a param that belongs elsewhere).

`flatten.rs` reports a diagnostic when this names a zone that did not reach the wire, because an extraction zone that does not exist is a round that can never be won that way (the same rule `$defs/vehicle.seats[].slotId` follows against the emitted slots). Read by `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator`, which resolves it through `TBD_ZoneRegistry` and refuses to evaluate rather than inventing a zone.

vipSlotId.description: `mode: vip` only — the `slots[].uid` of the protected player. Matched against the EMITTED slot uids by `flatten.rs`, not the authored ones, for the same reason `$defs/vehicle.seats[].slotId` is: a uid that resolves in the editor payload but that the compile emitted no `slots[]` row for would dangle on the wire. Read by `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator`.

timeoutMinutes.description:
`mode: timeout` only — how long the round runs before the clock ends it, in whole minutes. 1440 is 24 h; the ceiling exists for the same reason `$defs/zoneRules.captureSeconds` has one (a typo'd `600` where `60` was meant is a round nobody can finish).

It is NOT a second clock. `flatten.rs` projects it onto `flow.timeLimitSeconds` (× 60) and adds `time_limit` to `endOn`, so the round is ended by the ONE armed clock `TBD_FrameworkManager.ArmRoundClock` already runs. Two timers for one deadline is the T-946.19 defect class, and `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator` deliberately starts no timer of its own for this mode.

task.description: T-936.2 — one authored task. Transitions are assigned→succeeded and assigned→failed only; anything else is logged and ignored (server authoritative, `TBD_TaskStateMachine`). `triggerId` names an `editorTriggers[].id` whose T-676 completion drives the success transition. `markerId` is the HUD glyph: an authored `$defs/marker.icon` alias, resolved through `TBD_MarkerIcons` (the existing marker icon path). Position comes from the linked trigger's zone.

title.description: The words on the HUD marker and in the tasks panel.

state.description: Authoring default is `assigned`. The runtime writes the terminal state; the editor may also author a terminal state for a task that has already resolved in a canned scenario.

triggerId.description: Optional `editorTriggers[].id`. When that trigger fires, an `assigned` task becomes `succeeded`. An inert or missing trigger fails the task. Tasks observe; they never fire endOn.

markerId.description: Optional HUD icon alias from `$defs/marker.icon` (TBD_MarkerIcons.Register keys). Absent ⇒ the HUD uses `objective_marker`.

description.description: Optional longer briefing text. Not drawn on the HUD marker.

schedule.description: READ SINCE T-133 (2026-09-06). Optional timed window. Absent ⇒ untimed (always evaluate). `TBD_TaskStateMachine.c` reads nested `startAfterS`/`windowS` via the ABSENT sentinel; presence of the object is not a nested-ref test.

taskSchedule.description: T-133 — seconds from mission start (`startAfterS`) and duration (`windowS`). windowS must be > 0; startAfterS must be ≥ 0 and strictly inside mission length (enforced by tasks.rs; schema pins types and closed keys).

startAfterS.description: READ SINCE T-133 (2026-09-06). Seconds from mission start before the task becomes active. 0 is legal (evaluate from T+0).

windowS.description: READ SINCE T-133 (2026-09-06). Duration in seconds the task stays evaluable after startAfterS. Must be > 0.

icon.description: Authored marker glyph alias (T-276). CLOSED vocabulary matching the 64 Register() keys in TBD_MarkerIcons.EnsureAliases — the words a mission author / Mission Creator may type. Before this enum a typo or empty string validated clean and then DEGRADED at runtime: Resolve() returned FALLBACK_ICON (DOT) and logged once, so the marker still drew but not as authored. Live engine imageset-quad names (measured 91 at boot via GetIconEntries) may still resolve at RUNTIME via the config-quad path, but the *authored* contract is this enum only — documents that pass the validator never need the silent DOT downgrade.

size.description: T-673 (ATTR-FIELD-MRK-SIZE, schemaVersion 1.3). Marker icon/text scale multiplier (1 = default). READ SINCE T-673 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct` in `apps/mod/tbd-framework/Scripts/Game/TBD/Backend/TBD_MissionLoader.c`, packed onto the marker RPC xs-trailer and applied by `TBD_MarkerClient`. Entity OBJ-SIZE (T-681) is a different field and still unread.

rotationDeg.description: T-673 (ATTR-FIELD-MRK-ROTATION, schemaVersion 1.3). Marker rotation in degrees. READ SINCE T-673 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct` / `TBD_MarkerClient.SetRotation`.

shape.description: T-673 (ATTR-FIELD-MRK-SHAPE, schemaVersion 1.3). Icon-vs-AREA is Eden's entire second marker model, and this key is the ICON-side selector / authoring hint, NOT the geometry. PRECEDENCE (the one rule that resolves the two): if `area` (a `#/$defs/markerArea`) is present, this marker IS an area marker and `shape` is IGNORED — the authoritative extent is `area`, whose vocabulary (circle | polygon | rectangle | ellipse) is the superset that can actually express a rect/ellipse. If `area` is absent, this is an icon marker (draw the `icon` glyph). `icon` names the glyph marker; `rectangle`/`ellipse`/`polyline` are legacy shape hints subordinate to `area` (an author who sets `shape: "ellipse"` must also author an ellipse `area` for it to take effect — the reader reads `area`, and mismatches resolve in `area`'s favour by this rule). READ SINCE T-673 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.shape`. Area *fill* (brush over `area` geometry) is still not drawn — `SCR_MapMarkerBase` has no brush API; T-673 logs once and still draws the icon with authored colour/rotation/size/alpha.

brush.description: T-673 (ATTR-FIELD-MRK-BRUSH, schemaVersion 1.3). Area-marker fill brush (matches Eden's marker brush set). Meaningful only for a `shape` other than `icon`. READ SINCE T-673 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.brush` (bound and packed); fill is not yet painted on the map widget.

color.description: T-673 (ATTR-FIELD-MRK-COLOR, schemaVersion 1.3). Marker colour, same `#rrggbb` form as `faction.color`. READ SINCE T-673 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.color`; hex is mapped to the nearest `SCR_EScenarioFrameworkMarkerCustomColor` via `SetColorEntry`.

alpha.description: T-673 (ATTR-FIELD-MRK-ALPHA, schemaVersion 1.3). Marker opacity, 0 (transparent) → 1 (opaque). READ SINCE T-673 (2026-09-06) by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.alpha` / `TBD_StyledMapMarker` widget opacity.

area.description: T-673 (schemaVersion 1.3). The AUTHORITATIVE extent of an area marker: circle | polygon | rectangle | ellipse (`#/$defs/markerArea`, a superset of the zone `#/$defs/shape` that adds the rect/ellipse extents `shape`'s circle|polygon cannot express). PRECEDENCE: when `area` is present this marker is an AREA marker and `marker.shape` is ignored (the rule is stated once here and once on `shape`). Its circle/polygon arms speak the same geometry vocabulary as a zone, so an area marker and a zone stay comparable. On the wire only — lands under T-673.
